name: The Undead
description: You've made a pact with a powerful undead being, such as a vampire, lich, or mummy lord. This patron grants you power over death and undeath, allowing you to channel the chill of the grave and command the spirits of the dead.

features.name: Form of Dread
features.description: You can use a bonus action to transform into a terrifying visage of death. For 1 minute, you gain the following benefits: You gain temporary hit points equal to 1d10 + your warlock level. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack, you can force the target to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the target is frightened of you until the end of your next turn. You can transform a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Grave Touched
features.description: Your patron's power changes your body. You don't need to eat, drink, or breathe. In addition, once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack, you can change the damage type of the attack to necrotic damage. While you are in your Form of Dread, you can also change the damage type of any spell you cast to necrotic damage.

features.name: Necrotic Husk
features.description: Your body is suffused with necrotic energy. You have resistance to necrotic damage. In addition, when you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you can drop to 1 hit point instead, and each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you takes necrotic damage equal to your warlock level + your Charisma modifier. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

features.name: Spirit Projection
features.description: As an action, you can project your spirit from your body. Your body is unconscious and appears dead while your spirit is projected. Your spirit resembles a spectral version of your body and has the following statistics: It has 1 hit point and immunity to all damage except force damage. It can't take actions or cast spells. It can move through creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It has a flying speed of 40 feet and can hover. While projected, you can use your action to return to your body. Your body regains consciousness when your spirit returns to it. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

name: College of Spirits
description: Bards of the College of Spirits seek to tell the stories of those who have passed on, using their magic to channel the spirits of the dead. These bards are often found in graveyards, haunted houses, and other places where the dead linger.

features.name: Spiritual Focus
features.description: You employ tools that aid you in channeling spirits, such as a candle, crystal, or totem. When you cast a bard spell that deals damage or restores hit points while holding your spiritual focus, you can roll a d6 and add it to the roll. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Tales from Beyond
features.description: You can reach out to the spirits of the dead to tell you stories. As a bonus action, you can roll a d6 and add it to your next ability check, attack roll, or saving throw. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Spiritual Focus (Improved)
features.description: Your spiritual focus becomes more powerful. When you cast a bard spell that deals damage or restores hit points while holding your spiritual focus, you can roll a d8 instead of a d6 and add it to the roll.

features.name: Spirit Session
features.description: You can cast the speak with dead spell at will, without expending a spell slot. When you cast the spell in this way, you can ask the corpse up to seven questions, rather than five.

features.name: Mystical Connection
features.description: You can use your Tales from Beyond feature without expending a use of it. When you do so, you roll a d8 instead of a d6.
